feature.title: Desk school: why guidance matters more than the quarter
body: When a company reports, it tells you two things: how last quarter went, and what it expects next. The first is history. Analysts and management both know it going in, so it is mostly priced. The second, called guidance in a report, is new information about the future, and that is what moves the stock.

That is why a company can beat on revenue and still fall. If the Street expects $109 billion and the company reports $110 billion but guides next quarter below what analysts expect, the stock usually drops. Traders compare each number with consensus, the average analyst forecast, and with the unofficial 'whisper number' that big holders are really positioned for.

Tonight is the textbook case. Nvidia's own guide was about $108 billion and the Street sits near $109 billion, so the quarter should come in fine. The questions are the next-quarter outlook, gross margin, and whether an interim CEO sounds as confident as a founder. In an interview, say that: 'It's a guide-and-tone event more than a number event.'

stories.headline: Trump and Xi are expected to meet at APEC in Shenzhen this week, with the trade truce already extended
stories.dek: The two sides pushed the truce's expiry into January before the summit, so the meeting is about tone; big announcements are expected to wait.
tldr: Trump and Xi are expected to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen this week, their third meeting this year, per the South China Morning Post.
The US-China trade truce, due to lapse on November 10, was extended by two months to January 10, 2027, the paper reports.
Negotiators are still working on concrete deals, and major announcements are expected to wait for the G20, so the bar for a positive surprise is low.
whatHappened: China hosts this year's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, and the South China Morning Post reports that Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are expected to meet there, for the third time this year. A briefing from the advisory firm BowerGroupAsia puts the leaders' meeting on November 18 and 19. Vladimir Putin is also expected to attend.

The most market-sensitive item was settled in advance. The [[trade truce]] the two leaders struck in Busan last year was due to expire on November 10. After talks in September, both governments extended it by two months, to January 10, 2027, with China announcing its extension days after Washington did, the paper reports.

What is not settled is substance. Negotiators have been racing to line up concrete trade and investment deals, and the same reporting says the major [[deliverables]] are expected to wait for the G20. I could not confirm from a second outlet that Trump's attendance is final.
background: A truce here means each side suspends the tariffs and export restrictions it had threatened, for a fixed period. It is a pause, with an expiry date, and each extension resets the clock. That is why markets care about the date more than the photo: a lapse would bring back higher tariffs on Chinese goods and China's limits on exports such as rare earths, which feed into chip and auto supply chains.
APEC itself is a 21-economy forum that produces statements, not treaties. Its value to markets is the meetings on the sidelines.
whyItMatters: With the truce extended, the downside scenario (a lapse this month) is off the table, so the summit carries more [[headline risk]] than fundamental risk. The assets that move on US-China tone are semiconductors, industrial exporters, soybeans and the yuan. It also lands in the same week as Nvidia's earnings, and Nvidia's China data-center revenue is close to zero under export controls, so any hint on chip rules matters for that stock too.

grandLine.title: A Reverie where the big vote waits
grandLine.body: At the Reverie, the world's kings gather at Mary Geoise, and once in a long while they vote to abolish an entire system, as they did with the Seven Warlords. Most of the time it is speeches. Shenzhen looks like the speeches kind: the truce was renewed before anyone arrived, and the decisions that would change the rules are expected at a later table.

views.thesis: The extension was the news; the meeting just confirms a stable relationship.
views.argument: Both governments chose to extend before the summit, and this is the third leader meeting this year. That pattern says neither side wants a blow-up, so tariff risk stays priced out into January.

views.thesis: Nothing new is on offer, so the risks are one-sided.
views.argument: If the deliverables wait for the G20, a good meeting changes little, while a stumble on chips, rare earths or Taiwan would hit semis and exporters. The extension is only two months, so the cliff comes back in January.

interview.question: Trump and Xi meet this week. Does that change how you'd position?
interview.answer: Not much. The market-moving piece, the truce extension to January, already happened, so the meeting is headline risk more than a catalyst. I'd expect a constructive tone and few deliverables. I wouldn't chase China-sensitive names into it, because the upside is small and a bad headline on chips or rare earths cuts the other way. What would change my mind is a concrete tariff rollback or a longer truce, which would be a real change in the path.

followUp.question: Which assets are most sensitive to US-China headlines?
followUp.answer: Semiconductors and industrial exporters in equities, soybeans in commodities, and the offshore yuan in FX. Rare-earth supply is the channel that hits autos and chips.

keyTerms.definition: A time-limited agreement to suspend threatened tariffs and export restrictions. It has an expiry date and has to be extended or replaced.
keyTerms.example: The Busan truce was due to lapse on November 10 and now runs to January 10, 2027.

keyTerms.definition: The concrete, announceable outcomes of a summit, such as a purchase commitment or a tariff cut, as opposed to statements of intent.
The risk that a news headline moves a price sharply even when the underlying fundamentals have not changed.

stories.headline: Nvidia reports tonight with the first guide under Kress; the Street wants about $109 billion and steady margins
stories.dek: A day after the Nasdaq fell 2.5%, the first report since Huang resigned tests whether the AI trade's anchor holds. Results come after the close; the call is at 5:00 PM ET.
stories.updateNote: Now the lead: earnings are tonight. Rebuilt with the debate, an interview answer and a trade.
tldr: Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results tonight after the close (about 4:20 PM ET), with the call at 5:00 PM ET, per its SEC filing.
Guidance was about $108 billion of revenue, plus or minus 2%; analysts expect about $109 billion and adjusted EPS near $2.47.
It is the first report since Jensen Huang resigned; Colette Kress, CFO and interim CEO, has to defend a guide she set while wearing the other hat.
whatHappened: Nvidia kept its earnings date after last week's leadership change: results come tonight after the close, about 1:20 PM Pacific, with the call at 2:00 PM Pacific, according to the company's filing. Previews put [[consensus]] at roughly $109 billion of revenue and about $2.47 to $2.48 of adjusted earnings per share, against company [[guidance]] of about $108 billion, plus or minus 2%. Kress set that guidance as CFO and now has to defend it as interim CEO.

The stock slid again on Monday, down roughly 4% in afternoon trading by one report, as the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.49%. Analysts are watching [[gross margin]], which Kress said in August would bottom in the fourth quarter, supply commitments, and China, where data-center revenue is near zero.
background: Nvidia sets the tone for AI spending because its customers' capital budgets are its revenue. A beat matters less than the next quarter's guide, since the stock is priced on what comes next. Kress's August comments gave a map for tonight: margins bottom in the fourth quarter, and supply commitments rose to about $145 billion. She said both as CFO; tonight she has to say them as the person in charge.

The leadership change adds one new variable that a number can't settle: whether the board's search for a permanent CEO changes the strategy. Companies in this position usually keep guidance conservative and the message steady.
whyItMatters: Nvidia is the largest weight in the Nasdaq and the reference point for AI spending, so its outlook sets the tone for tech into year-end. After a three-day slide in the S&P 500, positioning is lighter, so a steady guide can produce a sharp relief rally and a weak one can accelerate the selloff. Watch [[implied volatility]] and the after-hours move.

views.camp: A steady guide holds the line
views.thesis: Kress keeps the outlook and the AI trade stabilizes.
views.argument: The business hasn't changed, demand is supply-limited, and the guide is set. A clean quarter plus a confident, conservative outlook is enough after a drop that already priced in worry.

views.thesis: The CEO exit changes how the market reads every number.
views.argument: With the founder gone, investors may want more than in-line: a raised guide, firmer margin comments and clarity on the CEO search. A merely steady report could still leave the stock lower.

interview.question: Nvidia reports tonight with an interim CEO. What are you watching, and how do you trade it?
interview.answer: I'd watch the guide for next quarter more than this one, because the stock trades on what's next. Then gross margin, since Kress said it bottoms in the fourth quarter, and any comment on the CEO search. I wouldn't take a directional view into the print; I'd use options sized to the implied move. What would change my mind is a cut to the outlook, which would tell me the AI trade is breaking rather than pausing.

followUp.question: Why does the guide matter more than the quarter?
followUp.answer: The quarter is already known to management and largely expected by the Street, so it's mostly priced. The guide is new information about future demand, which is what the stock's multiple depends on.

trade.idea: Nvidia earnings straddle sized to the implied move
trade.expression: Long a near-dated at-the-money straddle (call plus put at the same strike) expiring after the report
trade.rationale: If the stock moves more than the options imply, either on a strong guide or a cut, the straddle pays. It expresses that the reaction will be large without picking a direction.
risks: If the stock moves less than the implied move, the premium is lost to the drop in implied volatility after the print.
Implied volatility is already elevated after Monday's selloff, so the straddle is expensive.

keyTerms.definition: The average analyst forecast for a company's results; beating it is the baseline for a positive reaction.
keyTerms.example: About $109 billion of revenue for Nvidia this quarter.

keyTerms.definition: A company's own forecast of its future results. Markets often react more to the guide for the next quarter than to the quarter just reported.
keyTerms.example: Nvidia's guide was about $108 billion, plus or minus 2%.

keyTerms.definition: Revenue minus the direct cost of the product, as a share of revenue. A falling gross margin means each sale earns less profit.
keyTerms.example: Kress said in August that gross margin would bottom in the fourth quarter.

keyTerms.definition: The market's expected size of future price swings, backed out of option prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection, then usually drops after the event.

watchNext.what: Revenue, gross margin, the next-quarter guide and any CEO-search news.
How the stock and the Nasdaq trade the next morning.

stories.headline: COP31 enters its final week in Antalya with climate finance the main focus and no US delegation
stories.dek: About 190 countries are at the UN climate summit in Türkiye, which runs through Friday. Washington sent no officials for a second year.
tldr: The UN climate summit runs November 9–20 in Antalya, Türkiye, with representatives of about 190 countries.
The US sent no officials for the second straight year, after withdrawing from the Paris Agreement earlier in 2026.
whatHappened: COP31 opened in Antalya on November 9 and is scheduled to close on November 20. Türkiye's summit president, Murat Kurum, has said the aim is to turn earlier pledges into action, with financing the main focus. Leaders met in the first week; the second week is when negotiators try to settle a final text. The Trump administration did not send representatives.
whyItMatters: The outcome shapes how much public money flows to energy transition in developing countries, which matters for renewables, grid and nuclear suppliers. With the US absent, the weight of any deal falls on the EU, China and the host.

stories.headline: Nasdaq falls 2.5% and the S&P 500 drops 1.9% as AI stocks slide into Nvidia's first report without Huang
stories.dek: The S&P 500 lost a third straight session, closing at 7,416.59, and the Dow fell 1.4%. Defensive sectors held up while chips and AI names led the selloff.
tldr: Technology led the damage, with Nvidia the focus a day before its first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned; consumer staples and health care were the exceptions.
The Nasdaq's drop is bigger than all of last week's 2.3% gain, so the rebound that followed the Nasdaq's slide earlier this month is gone.
whatHappened: U.S. stocks sold off hard on Monday, with technology leading. The S&P 500 shed 145.08 points, or 1.92%, to 7,416.59, its third straight loss. The Nasdaq Composite fell 626.52 points, or 2.49%, to 24,509.76, and the Dow dropped 739.38 points, or 1.41%, to 51,608.17, per AP and CNBC closing reports. Those figures line up exactly with Friday's closes (7,561.67, 25,136.27 and 52,347.55). Reuters-based reports quoted smaller intraday declines at points during the session.

Reports pointed at chip and AI names and at Nvidia in particular. The stock was down roughly 4% in afternoon trading, according to one report, with investors reluctant to hold it into Tuesday's [[event risk]]: the first report under interim CEO Colette Kress. Rising bond yields were also cited as a weight. Consumer staples and health care were the exceptions, a classic [[risk-off]] pattern in which money moves toward defensive groups.
background: The Nasdaq has now handed back more than it gained last week, when it rose about 2.3%. That rebound followed the post-election correction, and it leaned on two things: falling oil and a cooler producer-price report. Both have faded. Nvidia, the biggest single weight in the Nasdaq, has also lost its CEO since then, so index moves track its stock more tightly than usual.
whyItMatters: When the largest AI stock is the swing factor, the next move depends on one report. A clean beat with steady guidance can unwind a lot of the fear quickly, because positioning is already lighter. A weak outlook would confirm the worry that the AI trade is cracking, and with the S&P 500 down three days in a row there is less cushion. Watch [[implied volatility]]: if option prices stay high after the report, the market is still braced for more.

grandLine.title: Aqua Laguna on Tuesday
grandLine.body: In Water 7 everyone knows the giant tidal wave Aqua Laguna is coming, and the city still has to evacuate to high ground. Monday looks like that evacuation: with Nvidia's report on a known date, many investors cut exposure before the wave rather than after new information arrived. That is why a scheduled event can drag prices down in the days before it.

views.thesis: This is positioning, not a verdict on AI.
views.argument: Nvidia's date is fixed and the CEO change adds uncertainty, so traders trimmed beforehand. If guidance holds, the selling reverses, because the fundamentals have not changed.

views.thesis: Three down sessions plus a CEO exit is a trend, not a blip.
views.argument: With yields rising and the AI leader leaderless, the easy money has been made. A merely in-line report may not be enough to restart the rally.

interview.question: The Nasdaq is down 2.5% the day before Nvidia reports. Do you buy it or wait?
interview.answer: I'd wait for the report. The move looks like pre-earnings de-risking, and the outcome is binary on guidance, so I'd rather not own the gap in either direction. If Kress holds the revenue guide and margins, I'd look to buy the dip in the leaders. What would change my mind is a cut to the outlook or a sign the board is reconsidering the plan, which would make me think the AI trade has broken rather than paused.

followUp.question: How would you express a view on the report without owning the stock?
followUp.answer: A put spread on the Nasdaq-100 caps the cost and the risk, while a straddle pays on a big move in either direction. Because option prices already reflect the event, I'd compare implied move against how far the stock has actually moved on past reports.

trade.expression: Long QQQ near-dated 5% out-of-the-money put, short a 10% out-of-the-money put (put spread)
trade.rationale: If Tuesday's report disappoints and the selloff extends, the spread pays off at a defined cost. Selling the lower put reduces the premium after a volatile day.
risks: A strong report or steady guidance sends the Nasdaq sharply higher and the premium is lost.
Implied volatility is already high, so the spread is more expensive than usual and a calm reaction erodes it.

keyTerms.definition: The chance that a known, scheduled event (earnings, a data release) moves a price sharply, so traders adjust positions before it.
keyTerms.example: Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close.

keyTerms.definition: A market mood where investors sell volatile assets such as tech and buy defensive ones such as staples, health care and Treasuries.
keyTerms.example: Staples and health care rose Monday while tech fell.

keyTerms.definition: The market's expected size of future price swings, backed out of option prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection.
keyTerms.example: Option prices on Nvidia and the Nasdaq-100 are the gauge for Tuesday's expected move.

stories.headline: Fed minutes arrive Wednesday after Waller said a 50bp hike should be considered in December
stories.dek: Waller backs at least 25 basis points and sees room for more if inflation stays hot. Hammack and Williams speak this week, and Chair Warsh gives no guidance.
tldr: Governor Christopher Waller said on Nov. 10 he would support a 25bp hike in December and that a larger move may be needed if core prices rise 0.3% or more.
The minutes of the October meeting come out Wednesday at 2:00 PM ET; Hammack and Williams are among the Fed speakers this week, per a Newsquawk schedule.
whatHappened: In a speech in London on Nov. 10, Waller said he would back a 25 basis point increase at the December meeting even if October inflation improves, and that a 50 basis point hike should be considered if core prices rose 0.3% or more from September. Core CPI rose 0.3% in October. Reuters contrasted his guidance with Chair Kevin Warsh's resistance to giving any rate-path guidance.
A Newsquawk schedule lists Hammack speaking Tuesday and Williams on Wednesday, the same day the minutes of the October meeting are due.
whyItMatters: The minutes show how many officials were open to a larger move. A division would keep 50bp alive; a consensus for 25 would pull it back. Rates are the channel that moves Nvidia's multiple, which is why Wednesday matters for tech.

stories.headline: Anthropic is set to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT; the debut date and pricing are not confirmed
stories.dek: The AI company filed its S-1 on Oct. 26. One IPO calendar points to trading this week, but I could not confirm the date.
tldr: Anthropic filed a Form S-1 and applied to list Class A shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.
One IPO calendar lists first trading for Nov. 19; I found no company confirmation, and the price range and size had not been set in the filing.
whatHappened: Anthropic filed its S-1 with the SEC on Oct. 26, saying it applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under ANT, per Decrypt and InvestingLive. The filing did not set a share count or price range. Reports put the target valuation near $2 trillion, which remains preliminary. ABC7 reports the company is set to make its market debut; one IPO calendar lists Nov. 19.
Disclosure: this paper is written by Claude, which Anthropic makes.
whyItMatters: A very large AI listing adds supply to a market that has just sold off in tech, and it competes for the same AI-focused money as Nvidia. Big IPOs also tend to mark the later part of a rally, so desks will watch pricing and the first-day move.
